description: A bread preparation made with veal, beef or ham or forcemeat, and bacon.

Let this mixture fry on a pan for a while; you may also add stewed and finely chopped mushrooms
Season with pepper, add two whole eggs, mix well and thin with beef broth as needed
Cut thin slices from veal leg, flatten with the back of a knife, season with pepper and salt

Make a gravy from the liquid and leftover forcemeat

Wine may also be added to the gravy if desired

steps: Soak a pound of codfish in a shallow gallon-sized dish of water for 3 to 4 hours or overnight if preparing for breakfast
Once soaked, transfer to another vessel, pour fresh cold water over it and bring to boil
When the fish boils, drain the water and let it cool
Remove the skin and bones carefully and flake the meat
Place the fish in another vessel, pour milk over it until covered, and bring to boil
Mix a heaping spoonful of butter with a heaping spoonful of flour and add this to the boiling milk while stirring constantly
Beat one or two eggs and add to the sauce, mix well and season with pepper to taste
If the fish was too much soaked, salt to taste

steps: Put 3 teaspoons of melted butter, 3 teaspoons of sugar and 5 egg yolks in a bowl, salt it, and add enough flour to make a batter like for dripping
Gradually fold in stiffly beaten egg whites from 5 eggs
Heat a piece of butter in a pan, pour some of the batter onto it and bake an omelette on both sides
Spread each one with filling of either milk cheese, apple, or grated bread, fold the omelettes and place them in a buttered baking dish
Put the dish in a hot oven and let the omelettes bake, pour a bit of milk in which you have beaten an egg yolk over them, and let everything bake for about 10 more minutes
Be careful that they do not dry out too much

title: Tvarohové Knedlíky (Cottage Cheese Dumplings)
description: Prepared with cottage cheese, groats, and butter.

ingredients.name: 1 quart fresh cottage cheese, well pressed
ingredients.sourceText: 1 quart fresh cottage cheese, well pressed

steps: Take 2 tablespoons of fresh butter and beat it well on a plate
Add 3 eggs to it and mix well
Then add about 1 quart of well-pressed fresh cottage cheese, salt it appropriately and mix well with the eggs and butter so that no lumps remain
Then add as much groats as possible so that you can make little dumplings from it
Make the little dumplings medium-sized so that they cook through sooner
Before putting them to boil, coat each one in flour and then put them in salted water to boil

The best pies however are made from butter dough

title: Třešňový Pudding (Cherry Pudding)
description: A pudding made with cherry, rolls, and ground almonds.
steps: Soak the crumb of three rolls in boiling milk, place in a mortar with {{source-2}} and stir until it becomes smooth dough.
Set aside, add a bit of finely chopped lemon zest, {{source-4}}, and let it cool.
Then add {{source-5}}, six egg yolks, and mix well together.

Take one pound of cherries, remove the pits, place the cherries in a mortar with a little wine and sugar, let them cook briefly, and place on a sieve so the juice drains, as otherwise the pudding would be heavy.
Add the cherries to the remaining mixture, mix carefully, and fold in snow made from six egg whites.
Grease a mold with butter, sprinkle with grated rolls, and let the pudding steam cook for three-quarters of an hour.
Remove onto a dish and pour cherry sauce over it.

title: Uherský guláš (Hungarian Gulash)
description: Prepared with beef, mutton, and pork.
steps: Cut beef, mutton, and pork meat into pieces.
Brown the chopped onion in bacon fat, add a little cumin and pepper.
Add the beef meat and let it braise while stirring frequently.
After a while, add the mutton meat and finally the pork.
Dust with flour, add beef broth or water, salt, paprika, several grains of allspice, and a little wine if desired.
Let it braise until everything is sufficiently tender.
Place the gulash in a deep platter and serve with boiled or fried potatoes.
Alternatively, peeled and chopped potatoes can be cooked with the meat.
For six people, 2-3 pounds of all meats combined is sufficient.

title: Vdolky (Filled Yeast Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with yeast, yeast or beer, and plum.
steps: Prepare the yeast: if using beer yeast, rinse with water until clear, then add a piece of sugar, a little milk and flour, and set in a warm place to ferment; if using pressed yeast, add water, milk, sugar and flour, and set in a warm place.
Sift 1 kilogram of flour. Cream 12 dekagrams (8 lots) of butter and add grated lemon peel.
Add most of the flour, incorporating 3 dekagrams (2 lots) of yeast, and add as much warm milk as the flour will absorb, working until the dough does not stick to the spoon.
Scrape down the mixing spoon and bowl, dust the dough with flour, set in a warm place and allow to ferment for about an hour.
Roll out the dough and cut vdolky with a small form or shape by hand.
Bake on a stove or on a greased sheet, or fry in butter like pastries.
Thin plum jam with water, add sugar, cinnamon or lemon peel, simmer briefly, and use to spread on the vdolky.
Sprinkle jam-topped vdolky with poppy seeds, gingerbread or cheese curds, and add a dollop of sour cream in the center.

title: Vejce vařená (Boiled Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs, water, and salt.
steps: For soft-boiled eggs where the white is partially cooked but not hard and the yolk is completely liquid, put clean washed eggs into boiling water, remove the pot from the heat so the water does not boil further, cover well and leave for five minutes
The best and safest method to achieve the desired degree of cooking is that the eggs are completely heated through and the white is nicely gelatinous and not hardened
Must be carefully watched and not left in water longer than five minutes
Another good method is to put eggs in cold water, bring to the fire and let the water come to a boil
As soon as the water begins to boil, the eggs are just right and the cook cannot be mistaken in this case
The most common method is to put eggs in boiling water and let them boil for three minutes
In this time they are soft-boiled
If we let them boil for five minutes, the white is cooked and the yolk is semi-liquid, whereas in 8 to 10 minutes they are hard-boiled

title: Vánočka (Christmas Twist)
description: Prepared with cloves or anise, yeast or sour cream or milk, and sultanas.

ingredients.name: two whole eggs or four yolks
ingredients.sourceText: two whole eggs or four yolks

ingredients.name: 1 small cup sugar dissolved in milk

ingredients.name: piece of pressed yeast, dissolved in sour cream or milk

steps: Put 8 small cups flour into a bowl, crumble half pound butter in it

Beat in two whole eggs or four yolks, add 1 small cup sugar dissolved in milk, a little grated lemon zest, salt, ground cloves or ground and sifted anise, a piece of pressed yeast dissolved in sour cream or milk and make the dough so thick as for dumplings
Beat it so long until it does not stick to the bowl or spoon, cover it with a warmed cloth, let it rise
Then add 1 small cup sultanas and half small cup chopped almonds
Then take the dough out onto a floured board, knead it again, divide it into four larger and five smaller pieces, let them rise a little more, then roll them out
From the first four make not too long a braid, place it on a sheet on paper brushed with butter
Make then a braid from three smaller pieces, place it straight on the first, press it on the ends
Finally twist two smallest pieces, place them on top of the second braid, arrange it nicely, press the ends together
Let the Christmas twist rise in warmth, then brush it with beaten egg and bake in moderate oven
If the Christmas twist is more risen, it must be baked at stronger heat
If you put whole eggs into the batter, it is more moist; with only yolks it is more porous; whole eggs are usually put into the Christmas twist

title: Zadělané Husí Drobečky s Knedličky (Goose Giblets with Quennelles)
description: Prepared with goose, vegetables, and goose liver.
steps: Salt and cook the goose giblets with vegetables like beef meat until tender.

Stir one large tablespoon of butter, beat in three eggs, add a small piece of finely chopped lemon peel, grated or chopped goose liver (if using chopped liver, remove the veins), salt lightly and mix well.
Add several tablespoons of good cream and enough grated bread or crackers to make quennelles.
If desired, add a small amount of chopped garlic with marjoram to the quenelle mixture and set aside.
Put a piece of fresh butter in a small pot and make a light roux, mix it with half of the strained broth from the giblets, and pour the other half of the broth also into the pot and let it boil.
Shape the mixture into round quennelles and cook them in the boiling broth.
When the quennelles are sufficiently cooked, add the cooked goose giblets to them, pour the reduced broth over, season lightly with nutmeg, and let simmer a little longer.
Remove the giblets, place them on a serving dish, arrange the quennelles around them, pour the sauce over and bring to the table.

Place the meat on a platter and prepare the sauce

title: Zapečené vepřové maso (Conserved Roast Pork)
description: Prepared with pork, salt, and caraway.
steps: When the meat from the slaughtered pig has cooled, slice it into neat pieces about half an inch thick
Remove all fat and bones
Salt the meat and let it lie in salt for at least one hour
Take a baking pan and lay the slices side by side on it
Sprinkle with caraway
Bake without adding any water until done
Remove the slices and lay them on a platter again side by side
When everything is done, let the meat cool
Take a large clay pot and pack the meat tightly into it
Pour lard over it so that the lard reaches two inches above the meat
When removing it, take care not to damage the pieces that are to remain in the pot; therefore it is best to remove more meat at once and pour the remainder well with lard so that air cannot reach it

title: Zavařená Jablka (Preserved Apples)
description: Prepared with apples, sugar, and water.

ingredients.name: beautiful, juicy apples, preferably sweet rather than sour
ingredients.sourceText: beautiful, juicy apples, preferably sweet rather than sour

steps: First the apples must be beautiful, juicy, preferably sweet rather than sour.
Peel them, cut into quarters, remove the cores well and anything that is spoiled; if the apple is quite large, cut it into more pieces and immediately throw them into cold water so they do not brown.
When finished with this, put a pot on the stove, add water according to the amount of fruit and for one gallon of water add about one quart of sugar and let it boil.
Then skim the foam and add the fruit and add a few pieces of broken cinnamon bark and let them boil until they can be easily pierced with a fork.
Then immediately pour into prepared jars which you have previously washed well with hot water and then cold water.
Most importantly, the lids must be well washed, particularly those that have been used before. Boil them in soda water, then rinse in several clean waters and if anything is stuck on, scrape it well.
Also each time when filling use new rubber strips.
